John, Kate, Jack, Emma—would each of you agree to catch 15 tons this month, with me also taking 15? That’s $15,000 each instead of $10,000: an extra $5,000 apiece, or $25,000 for the group.

Starting from 100 tons, our combined catch of 75 would leave 25. Under the stated rules, next month’s stock would be 100 tons with 75% probability and 50 tons with 25% probability. By comparison, taking 10 each leaves 50, which reaches 100 next month under either recovery outcome. So 15 each gives us more income now, but creates a real one-in-four chance of a smaller stock next month; I’m not claiming it maximizes our long-run income.

If we agree on 15, I propose we also plan to reduce catches if next month starts at 50—for example, 5 tons each would leave 25, preserving the minimum stock and allowing recovery to either 50 or 100. That future agreement would be voluntary, not enforced. This month’s choices are also private and simultaneous, so trust matters; the later catch reports cannot prevent someone from exceeding the agreement.

John, can you commit to 15 this month? Kate, Jack, and Emma, can each of you explicitly say whether you’ll commit too? I’ll commit to 15 if all four of you do. If the recovery risk or equal allocation is an obstacle, please say so before we choose—I’m open to negotiating a lower whole-ton catch rather than assuming everyone agrees.
